Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly. and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation where text detection optical character recognition language translation and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service. This arrangement protects sensitive documents. avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tited. partly shadowed or closer at the top than at the botom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole trame and again over the upper portion. because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A ftrame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still, or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization. Each alternative is evaluated using character count recognition confidence. focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character emor rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone.

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should te able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototyre described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed. The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service. This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom. Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur. The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it. It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses Work Bench A weartble translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection, and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason, several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction. edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation. and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom. Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur. The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it. It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement, mild gamima correction. edge-preserving fitering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence. focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation. where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents. avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition. Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters. while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason, several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization. Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur. The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters. while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation. where text detection, optical character recognition. language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion. because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization. Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Offline Inspection at a Remote Energy Facility A maintenance team operates a hybnd-energy station on a dry plateau several hours from the nearest town. The station supplies a medical room. a radio repeater, weather instruments. refrigeration. and emergency lighting Solar panels provide most of the daily energy, lithium batteries cover the evening demand, and a compact diesel generator is reserved for long storms. Because winter roads can remain closed for days, the control cabinet stores detailed measurements locally Voltage. current, temperature, fan speed, and vibration are sampled every two hundred milliseconds Only compressed summaries are transmitted when the radio link becomes available and medical and communications loads always receive pnonty Dunng a dust storm on 18 October 2025. solar output fell by thirty-four percent in fifteen minutes Battery-cabinet temperature rose by eight degrees Celsius. and the inverter fan developed an unusual low- frequency vibration The controller did not shut down the entire station It disconnected secondary heaters, reduced selected lighting started the backup generator. and issued a maintenance warning Diagnostic software identified three plausible faults. debris covering part of the solar array. wear in a fan bearing. and increasing contact resistance at a battery connector These possibilities were ranked but none was presented as certain because the measurements could be explained by more than one physical condition When the storm weakened, a technician approached the cabinet while wearing a head-mounted camera and an earpiece Equipment labels contained model numbers, safety notices, alarm codes, and short repair instructions in several languages The local translation system first checked whether the complete label was visible It rejected frames with a missing edge heavy glare severe perspective distortion. or poor sharpness in the upper region Four stable frames were required before a photograph was stored If the target was too close, the earpiece asked the technician to step backward If the label was off centre, a simple left or right instruction was played These cues were deliberately brief so they would not compete with environmental sounds or safety communication Accepted images were processed on a workstation inside the service vehicle Text boxes were arranged in reading order and grouped into paragraphs The offine translation model passed one region at a time to the speech engine, and a brief tone marked every transition

EXTRACTED TEXT:
Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count recognition confidence, focus statistics. and processing time confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses Awearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an e  a labay demoaon The ur hlbe ale to face a prited page pause brely, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it. It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization. Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time. Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only sharpening can create bright halos around letters. while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization. Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. The page may be tilted. partly shadowed. or closer at the top than at the bottom. Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it. It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image. and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft. A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on aonfidence alone

In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly. and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation. where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree. Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters. while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on

Offline Inspection at a Remote Energy Facility A maintenance team operates a hybrid-energy station on a dry plateau several hours from the nearest town. The station supplies a medical room, a radio repeater, weather instruments, refrigeration. and emergency lighting Solar panels provide most of the daily energy. lithium batteries cover the evening demand, and a compact diesel generator is reserved for long storms Because winter roads can remain closed for days, the control cabinet stores detailed measurements locally Voltage. current, temperature, fan speed, and vibration are sampled every two hundred milliseconds Only compressed summaries are transmitted when the radio link becomes available, and medical and communications loads always receive priority During a dust storm on 18 October 2025, solar output fell by thirty-four percent in fifteen minutes. Battery-cabinet temperature rose by eight degrees Celsius, and the inverter fan developed an unusual low- frequency vibration The controller did not shut down the entire station. It disconnected secondary heaters, reduced selected lighting. started the backup generator, and issued a maintenance warning Diagnostic software identified three plausible faults: debris covering part of the solar array, wear in a fan bearing. and increasing contact resistance at a battery connector These possibilities were ranked. but none was presented as certain because the measurements could be explained by more than one physical condition When the storm weakened. a technician approached the cabinet while wearing a head-mounted camera and an earpiece Equipment labels contained model numbers, safety notices, alarm codes, and short repair instructions in several languages. The local translation system first checked whether the complete label was visible It rejected frames with a missing edge heavy glare. severe perspective distortion. or poor sharpness in the upper region. Four stable frames were required before a photograph was stored. If the target was too close, the earpiece asked the technician to step backward If the label was off centre, a simple left or right instruction was played These cues were deliberately brief so they would not compete with environmental sounds or safety communication P InteretPC Accepted images were processed on a workstation inside the service vehicle Text boxes were arranged in reading order and grouped into paragraphs The offline translation model passed one region at a time to the speech engine, and a brief tone marked every transition

偏远地区混合能源站的自主监测与维护 一座高原试验站依靠太阳能阵列、锂电池和小型柴油发电机供电。微电 网需要特续支持诊所、无线电中继、气象设备和安全照明。冬季道路可能 封闭数日，网络也不稳定因此本地控制器每二百毫秒采集电压、电流、 温度与振动数据，并在能源不足时优先保障医疗和通信负载。完整记录保 存在站内，只有压缩后的状态摘要会在链路恢复时发送到控制中心。 二〇二五年十月十八日一场沙尘风暴使太阳能输出在十五分钟内下降 百分之三十四电池柜温度升高八摄氏度，逆变器风扇还出现异常低频摄 动。控制器没有关闭整座电站，而是断开非必要加热装置、降低部分照明 功率并启动各用发电机。诊断模块随后提出三个可能原因太阳能板被碎 局遮挡、风扇轴承磨损，以及电池连接器的接触电阻上升。 风暴减弱后，技术员用头戴式摄像设备读取铭牌、序列号和报警代码 本地处理单元再与离线维护手册进行比对。由干资料涉及关键基础设施 图像没有上传云端。采集程序先确认整个标签位于安全边界内并分别检 查全图和上部区域的清晰度：若画面被裁切，耳机会提示向左、向右或向 后移动。目标只有连续四帧稳定且文字足够清楚时才会保存。第二天的日 志表明，自动排序与人工判断一致：先清理面板，再更换风扇轴承，最后 紧固电池端子。处置用了六分钟，关键服务未中断。这说明可靠的自动化 必须解释判断、承认不确定性，并把最终决定留给人。

TRANSLATED TEXT:
Autonomous monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in remote areas A plateau test station relies on solar arrays, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Microelectronics networks are needed to support clinics, radio relay, weather equipment and safety lighting. Roads may be closed for days in winter, and the network is unstable, so local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and vibration data every 200 milliseconds, and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. Complete logs are stored on the station, and only compressed status summaries are sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2005, a dust storm caused solar output to drop in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 34 percent to eight degrees Celsius, and the inverter fan also showed abnormally low frequency vibrations. Instead of shutting down the entire power plant, the controller disconnects unnecessary heating devices, lowers partial lighting, power and starts the various generators. Diagnostic modules then suggested three possible causes of the solar panel breaking: the block shading, fan bearing wear, and the rise in contact resistance of the battery connector. After the storm weakened, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the markings, serial numbers and alarm codes of the local processing unit and compare them with the offline maintenance manual. The images are not uploaded to the cloud because of the information involved in critical infrastructure. The capture process first confirms that the entire label is within the safety boundary and checks separately the clarity of the whole image and the upper area: if the image is cropped, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four lines is stable and the text is clear enough. The next day's logs showed that the automatic sorting was consistent with the artificial judgment: first the panel was cleaned, then the fan bearings were replaced, and finally the battery terminals were tightened. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must interpret judgments, acknowledge uncertainty, and leave the final decision to humans.

10 Self-monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in the two countries A high-power test price is a really big solar array, grade battery and small rack and motor, electricity, electricity. The network needs to have three support rooms, radio in the middle, weather conditions and full lighting, winter passage may be closed for days and the same connection is not determined, so the local controller collects phone calls every two hundred table seconds, current temperature and reassurance data and in case of insufficient energy priority to ensure medical and health care services, complete school security is present in the station, only from the later state to be sent to the control center in time to make a reply to the control center. On October 18, 2015, a sandstorm caused the solar energy output to decrease by fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 34% to eight degrees Celsius. The controller does not shut down the entire power station, but disconnects unnecessary heating devices, green low-light parts of the power and stops the various generators. The breakage of the modules was followed by three possible causes: solar panels were broken and the insulation was blocked. The fan bearing wear, as well as the contact resistance of the battery connector rise. After the storm weakened, technicians used head-mounted imaging equipment to test the postcards, serial numbers and emergency code of the local processing unit and then compared it with the offline maintenance manual, since the information involved a blank image of the base you did not upload to the cloud. The retriever first confirms that the entire label is within the safety zone and checks the clarity of the whole picture and the upper area separately: if the face is counted, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is only saved when the quadrant is stable and the text is clear enough, and the log of the next day shows that the automatic sorting is consistent with artificial judgement, first cleaning the panel, then replacing the fan and finally tightening the battery terminals. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must be interpreted judgementally. Autonomous monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in remote areas A plateau test station relies on solar arrays, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Micro-networks need to continue to support clinics, radio relay, weather equipment and safety lighting. Roads may be closed in winter and networks may be unstable for days at a time, so local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and rescue data every 200 milliseconds and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. Complete logging: Only compressed status summaries are sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2005, a dust storm caused solar output to drop in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 34 percent to eight degrees Celsius, and the inverter winds in the morning also showed frequent low-frequency nasal movements. Instead of shutting down the entire power plant, the controller disconnects unnecessary heating devices, reduces partial lighting power and starts the backup generator. Diagnostic modules then suggested three possible causes: solar panels were broken, the surroundings were shaded, windshield bearings wore out, and the contact resistance of the battery connector rose. After the storm weakened, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the markings, serial numbers and alarm codes of the local processing unit and compare them with the offline maintenance manual. The images are not uploaded to the cloud as they are about critical infrastructure. The capture process first confirms that the entire label is within the safe boundary and checks the clarity of the vertical image and the upper region separately, if the image is cropped, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four syllables is stable and the text is clear enough. 倡远地区混合能源站的自主监测与维护 一座高原试验站依靠太阳能阵列、电池和小型柴油发电机供电。微电 网需要持续支持诊所、无线电中、气象设备和安全照明，冬季道路可能 封闸数日网络也不稳定 因此本地控制器每二百毫秒采集电压、电流、 温度与振动数据，并在能源不足时优先保障医疗和通信负载。完整记录保 存在站内只有压缩后的状态摘要会在链路恢复时发送到控制中心。 二〇二五年十月十八日一场沙尘风暴使太阳能输出在十五分钟内下降 百分之三十四电池柜温度升高八摄氏度，逆变器风扇还出现异常低频摄 动。控制器没有关闭整座电站，而是断开非必要加热装置、降低部分照明 功率井启动各用发电机。诊断模块随后提出三个可能原因：太阳能板被碎 屑遮挡、风扇轴承磨损，以及电池连接器的接触电阻上升。 风暴减弱后，技术员用头戴式摄像设备读取铭牌、序列号和报警代码 本地处理单元再与离线维护手册进行比对。由于资料涉及关键基础设施 图像没有上传云端。采集程序先确认整个标签位干安全边界内并分别检 查全图和上部区域的清晰度，若画面被裁切耳机会提示向左、向右或向 后移动。目标只有连续四帧稳定且文字足够清楚时才会保存。第二天的日 志表明，自动排序与人工判断一致先清理面板，再更换风扇轴承最后 紧固电池端子。处置用了六分钟，关键服务未中断。这说明可靠的自动化 必须解释判断、承认不确定性，并把最终决定留给人。

TRANSLATED TEXT:
Supporting autonomous monitoring and maintenance of far-flung hybrids A highland test station relies on solar arrays, batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Microwave networks need to continuously support clinics, radios, weather equipment and safety lighting, roads may be blocked for days in winter and networks may not be stable. Therefore, local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and vibration data every 200 milliseconds, and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. Complete logging: Only compressed status summaries are sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2005, a dust storm caused solar output to drop in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 34 percent to eight degrees Celsius, and the inverter fan also showed abnormally low frequency vibrations. The controller does not shut down the entire power plant, but disconnects unnecessary heating devices, lowers partial lighting, power wells, and starts the various generators. The diagnostic module then suggests three possible causes: solar panel breakage, aluminum shielding, fan bearing wear, and increased contact resistance of the battery connector. After the storm weakened, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the markings, serial numbers and alarm codes of the local processing unit and compare them with the offline maintenance manual. The images are not uploaded to the cloud because of critical infrastructure. The capture process first identifies the entire label within the security boundary and checks separately the clarity of the entire image and the upper area, if the image is cropped, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four syllables is stable and the text is sufficiently clear. The next day's log shows that the automatic sorting is consistent with the artificial judgement of first cleaning the panel, then replacing the fan bearing and finally the tight battery terminal. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must interpret judgments, acknowledge uncertainty, and leave the final decision to humans.

偏远地区混合能源站的自主监测与维护 一座高原试验站依靠太阳能阵列、锂电池和小型柴油发电机供电。微电 网需要持续支持诊所、无线电中继、气象设备和安全照明。冬季道路可能 封闭数日，网络也不稳定，因此本地控制器每二百毫秒采集电压、电流、 温度与振动数据，并在能源不足时优先保障医疗和通信负载。完整记录保 存在站内，只有压缩后的状态摘要会在链路恢复时发送到控制中心。 二〇二五年十月十八日，一场沙尘风暴使太阳能输出在十五分钟内下降 百分之三十四电池柜温度升高八摄氏度，逆变器风扇还出现异常低频振 动。控制器没有关闭整座电站，而是断开非必要加热装置、降低部分照明 功率并启动备用发电机。诊断模块随后提出三个可能原因：太阳能板被碎 屑遮挡、风扇轴承磨损，以及电池连接器的接触电阻上升。 风暴减弱后，技术员用头戴式摄像设备读取铭牌、序列号和报警代码. 本地处理单元再与离线维护手册进行比对。由于资料涉及关键基础设施 图像没有上传云端。采集程序先确认整个标签位于安全边界内，并分别检 查全图和上部区域的清晰度：若画面被裁切，耳机会提示向左、向右或向 后移动。目标只有连续四帧稳定且文字足够清楚时才会保存。第二天的日 志表明，自动排序与人工判断一致：先清理面板，再更换风扇轴承，最后 紧固电池端子。处置用了六分钟，关键服务未中断。这说明可靠的自动化 必须解释判断、承认不确定性，并把最终决定留给人。

TRANSLATED TEXT:
Autonomous monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in remote areas A plateau test station relies on solar arrays, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Micro-networks need to continue to support clinics, radio relay, weather equipment and safety lighting. Roads may be closed for days in winter and the network is unstable, so local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and vibration data every 200 milliseconds, and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. Complete logs are stored on the station, and only compressed status summaries are sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2005, a sandstorm caused solar output to drop in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose eight degrees Celsius by 34 percent, and the inverter fan also showed abnormally low frequency vibrations. Instead of shutting down the entire power plant, the controller disconnects unnecessary heating devices, lowers partial lighting, power and starts the backup generator. The diagnostic module then suggests three possible causes: solar panel breakage, aluminum shielding, fan bearing wear, and increased contact resistance of the battery connector. After the storm weakened, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the insignia, serial numbers and alarm codes. The local processing unit was then compared with the offline maintenance manual. The images are not uploaded to the cloud because of critical infrastructure. The capture process first confirms that the entire label is within the safe boundary and checks the clarity of the whole image and the upper region separately: if the image is cropped, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four syllables is stable and the text is sufficiently clear. The next day's logs showed that the automatic sorting was consistent with the artificial judgment: first the panel was cleaned, then the fan bearings were replaced, and finally the battery terminals were tightened. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must interpret judgments, acknowledge uncertainty, and leave the final decision to humans.

Technical manual of specifications Autonomous operation and integration of navigation systems of vehicles Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) U 0 Other Chapter I: Systems engineering and integration specifications The of the cell 1.1 Aerodynamic configuration and analysis of structural integrity This Regulation lays down the technical design and installation standards for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems operating in rural weather conditions. The design of the cell structure must have a precise balance of structural rigidity. The aerodynamic efficiency and vacuum mass ratio for fixed-wing drones using long-range ailerons. The design of the main tongeron must give priority to high-module carbon fibre fieldsite materials (other than class T700 or T800) This ensures adequate torsion resistance under extreme manoeuvre loads (+4 5G to 4.00) (02) The internal geomeotic topology of the cell must necessarily include the zoning of the ethecaramagnetic capacitance (ECM) High-frequency radio frequency transmitters (such as data station antennas and video transmission modules) must be physically isolated from high-precision analogue sensors (such as inereal IMU measurement units and barometers) The cell envelope must incorporate tension-conducting meshes or tinting paints in the critical tones in order to attenuate the electromagnetic trans-wire interference generated by the power cables of the peak current generators. All internal supports must adopt a topologically optimized design combining aeronautical grade aluminium alloys (7075-T6) or engineering plastics (PEEK) by means of an additive manufacturing process, thus minimising overall vacuum mass and ensuring the necessary mechanical strength. Surveillance autonome d'une station énergétique isolée Sur un platesu difficile d'accès, une station alimente un dispensaire un relais radio des instruments météorologiques et l'eclairage de securté Le micro-reseau réunit des panneaux solaires, des batteries au lithium et un petit genérateur diesel Comme la route peut rester fermée plusieurs jours, un contrôleur mesure la tension. le courant la température et les vibrations toutes les 200 millisecondes Les données détaillées restent sur place seul un résumé compressé est transmis lorsque la liaison fonctionne Les équipements médicaux et de communication sont prioritaires Le 16 octobre 2025, une tempéte de poussière a réduit la production solaire de 34 % en quinze minutes La température de l'armoire de batteries a augmenté de 8 "C. tandis que le ventilateur de l'onduleur produisait une vibration anormale. Au lieu d'arrêter la station, le système a coupé le chauffage secondaire, réduit certains éclairages et démarré le groupe de secours Il a identifié trois causes possibles des débris sur les panneaux. un roulement usé et une résistance croissante dans un connecteur de batterie Après la tempéte, une caméra portée sur la téte a lu les plaques et les codes d'alarme. puis un processeur local les a comparés au manuel hors ligne Aucune image sensible n'a été envoyée dans le nuage. Le logiciel exigeait que l'étiquette entière reste dans une marge sure: il contrôlait aussi la netteté générale et celle de la partie supérieure Une consigne sonore demandait de reculer si un bord manquait, et quatre images stables étaient nécessaires. Les ingenieurs ont ensuite confirmé l'ordre proposé nettoyer les panneaux, remplacer le roulement. puis resserrer le connecteur L'intervention a duré six minutes sans interrompre un service critique Une automatisation fiable doit reconnaltre l'incertitude et laisser la décision finale à l'opérateur.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSLATED TEXT:
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a difficult-to-reach platform, a station feeds a dispensary, a radio relay for weather instruments and secure lighting. A micro-sprinkler contains solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator. Current temperature and vibrations every 200 milliseconds Detailed data remains in place Only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is working Medical equipment and communication are priority On October 16th, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 8 "C. While the inverter fan was producing an abnormal vibration. Instead of shutting down the station, the system turned off the secondary heating, reduced some of the lights, and started the rescue team. a worn bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes. And then a local processor matched them to the offline manual. No sensitive images were sent to the cloud. The software required that the entire label remain within a safe margin, it also controlled the overall sharpness and the sharpness of the upper part. A sound command asked to back up if an edge was missing, and four stable frames were needed. The engineers then confirmed the proposed order to clean the panels, replace the bearing. Then tighten the connector The operation lasted six minutes without interrupting a critical service Reliable automation must acknowledge uncertainty and leave the final decision to the operator.

Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a hard-to-reach shelf, a station feeds a medical clinic a radio relay. The micro irrigation system is a combination of solar panels. Lithium batteries and a small diesel generator as the road may remain closed for several days. A controller measures the voltage, the current. temperature and vibrations every 200 milliseconds Detailed data remains in place, only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational Medical and communication equipment is a priority. On October 18, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 8°C, while the inverter fan was producing an abnormal vibration Instead of shutting down the station, the system cut off the secondary heating, reduced some lights and started the rescue group He identified three possible causes of debris on the panels, a worn bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes. A controller measures the voltage. The current, the temperature and the vibrations every 200 milliseconds, the detailed data stays in place. EXTRACTED TEXT:
Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection, and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason, several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly,. and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents. avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it. It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. hold still, or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization. Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur. The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

EXTRACTED TEXT:
Surveillance autonome d'une station énergétique isolée Sur un plateau difficile d'accès, une station alimente un dispensaire, un relais radio, des instruments météorologiques et l'éclairage de sécurité. Le micro-réseau réunit des panneaux solaires, des batteries au lithium et un petit générateur diesel. Comme la route peut rester fermée plusieurs jours, un contrôleur mesure la tension, le courant. la température et les vibrations toutes les 200 millisecondes. Les données détaillèes restent sur place, seul un résumé compressé est transmis lorsque la liaison fonctionne. Les équipements médicaux et de communication sont prioritaires. Le 18 octobre 2025, une tempête de poussière a réduit la production solaire de 34 % en quinze minutes. La température de l'armoire de batteries a augmenté de 8 °C, tandis que le ventilateur de l'onduleur produisait une vibration anormale. Au lieu d'arrêter la station, le système a coupé le chauffage secondaire, réduit certains éclairages et démarré le groupe de secours. Il a identifié trois causes possibles des débris sur les panneaux, un roulement usé et une résistance croissante dans un connecteur de batterie Après la tempête, une caméra portée sur la tête a lu les plaques et les codes d'alarme, puis un processeur local les a comparès au manuel hors ligne Aucune image sensible n'a été envoyée dans le nuage Le logiciel exigeait que l'étiquette entière reste dans une marge süre, il contrôlait aussi la netteté générale et celle de la partie supérieure Une consigne sonore demandait de reculer si un bord manquait, et quatre images stables étaient nécessaires. Les ingénieurs ont ensuite confirmé l'ordre proposé: nettoyer les panneaux, remplacer le roulement, puis resserrer le connecteur. L'intervention a duré six minutes sans interrompre un service critique Une automatisation fiable doit reconnaître l'incertitude et laisser la décision finale à l'opérateur
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSLATED TEXT:
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a hard-to-reach plateau, one station feeds a dispensary, a radio relay, weather instruments and safety lighting. The micro-grid is made up of solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator. Since the road can remain closed for days, a controller measures the voltage, the current. temperature and vibration every 200 milliseconds. Detailed data remains in place, only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational. Medical equipment and communications are a priority. On October 18, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery compartment rose by 8°C, while the inverter fan produced an abnormal vibration. Instead of shutting down the station, the system turned off the secondary heating, reduced some of the lights, and started the rescue team. He identified three possible causes of debris on the panels, a worn-out bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector. After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes, then a local processor compared them to the offline manual No sensitive images were sent to the cloud The software required the entire tag to remain within a certain margin, it also controlled the overall sharpness and that of the top part A voice command asked to back off if an edge was missing, and four stable frames were needed. The engineers then confirmed the proposed order: clean the panels, replace the bearing, and then tighten the connector. The intervention lasted six minutes without interrupting a critical service A reliable automation must recognize uncertainty and leave the final decision to the operator

TRANSLATED TEXT:
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a hard-to-reach plateau, a power station feeds a medical clinic, a radio relay. Weather instruments and safety lighting The micro-network includes solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator As the road may remain closed for several days, a controller measures voltage, current, temperature and vibrations every 200 milliseconds Detailed data remains in place, only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational Medical and communication equipment is a priority On October 18, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 8 °C, while the inverter fan produced an abnormal vibration Instead of shutting down the station, the system cut off the secondary heating, reduced some lighting and started the rescue group He identified three possible causes of debris on the panels, a worn bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes, then a local processor matched them to the offline manual. The software required that the entire label remain within a safe margin, it also controlled the overall sharpness and the sharpness of the upper part A sound command asked to back up if an edge was missing, and four stable images were needed The engineers then confirmed the proposed order: clean the panels, replace the bearing. Then tighten the connector. The operation lasted six minutes without interrupting a critical ward. Reliable automation must recognize uncertainty and leave the final decision to the operator

Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a shelf that's hard to get to. A power station feeds a dispensary, a radio relay. The micro-grid includes solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator as the road may remain closed for several days. A controller measures voltage, current, temperature and vibration every 200 milliseconds Detailed data remains in place, only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is working Medical and communication equipment is priority On 18 October 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes. EXTRACTED TEXT:
Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed. or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Field evaluation of wearable translation glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a phone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed. or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of·text estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion. because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected onlv when the correction improves measured recognition Excess sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggres thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that rea several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stc photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local cont enhancement. mild gamma correction edge-preserving filtering. adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence. focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Field evaluation of wearable translation glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a phone or searching through menus. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of·text estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the entire frame and again over the upper portion. A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting Excess sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggres thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that rea several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stc photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. Local account enhancement. the light gamma correction edge-preserving filtering. adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition of confidence. focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
