EXTRACTED TEXT:
Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service. This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable intemet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed. or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Field evaluation of wearable translation glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a phone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed. This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable intemet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partially shadowed. Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition. Several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONSERVATIVELY CORRECTED TEXT:
Field evaluation of wearable translation glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a phone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed. This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partially shadowed. Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition. Several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right hold still. or improve the lighting when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation. where text detection, optical character recognition language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale. local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection, and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. The page may be tilted. partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur. The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason, several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering, and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

The page may be tilted. Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur. The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason, several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. Les données détaillées restent sur place, seul un résume compressé est transmis lorsque la liaison fonctionne Les équipements médicaux et de communication sont prioritaires Le 18 octobre 2025, une tempête de poussière a réduit la production solaire de 34 % en quinze minutes La température de l'armoire de batteries a augmenté de 8 C. tandis que le ventilateur de londuleur produisait une vibration anormale Au lieu d'arrêter la station, le systeme a coupé le chauffage secondaire, réduit certains éclairages et demarre le groupe de secours ll a identifié trois causes possibles des debris sur les panneaux, un roulement usé et une résistance croissante dans un connecteur de batterie Après la tempête, une caméra portée sur la tête a lu les plaques et les codes d'alarme, puis un processeur local les a comparés au manuel hors ligne Aucune image sensible n'a été envoyée dans le nuage Le logiciel exigeait que l'étiquette entière reste dans une marge süre: il contrôlait aussi la netteté générale et celle de la partie supérieure Une consigne sonore demandait de reculer si un bord manquait et quatre images stables étaient nécessaires Les ingenieurs ont ensuite confirmé l'ordre propose nettoyer les panneaux, remplacer le roulement. puis resserrer le connecteur L'intervention a duré six minutes sans reconnaitre lincertitude et laisser la décision finale à l opérateur

TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a difficult-to-reach plateau, a station feeds a dispensary a radio relay, weather instruments and safety lighting The micro-network includes solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator As the road may remain closed for several days, a controller measures the voltage. The current temperature and vibrations every 200 milliseconds. Detailed data remains in place, only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is working Medical and communication equipment is a priority On October 18, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes. Instead of shutting down the station, the system turned off the secondary heating, reduced some of the lights and started the rescue team. It identified three possible causes of debris on the panels, worn bearings and increasing resistance in a battery connector. After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the plates and alarm codes, then a local processor compared them to the offline manual No sensitive image was sent to the cloud The software required the entire tag to remain within a certain timeframe: it also controlled the overall sharpness and that of the top part A voice command asked to back off if an edge was missing and four stable images were needed The engineers then confirmed the order to clean the panels, replace the bearing. Then tighten the connector The operation lasted six minutes without acknowledging the uncertainty and leaving the final decision to the operator

Surveillance autonome d'une station énergétique isolée Sur un plateau difficile d'accès, une station alimente un dispensaire, un relais radio, des instruments météorologiques et l'éclairage de sécurité. Le micro-réseau réunit des panneaux solaires, des batteries au lithium et un petit générateur diesel Comme la route peut rester fermée plusieurs jours un contrôleur mesure la tension, le courant, la température et les vibrations toutes les 200 millisecondes Les données détaillées restent sur place; seul un résumé compressé est transmis lorsque la liaison fonctionne. Les équipements médicaux et de communication sont prioritaires. Le 18 octobre 2025, une tempête de poussière a réduit la production solaire de 34 % en quinze minutes La température de l'armoire de batteries a augmenté de 8 °C, tandis que le ventilateur de l'onduleur produisait une vibration anormale Au lieu d'arrêter la station, le système a coupé le chauffage secondaire, réduit certains éclairages et démarré le groupe de secours. Il a identifié trois causes possibles des débris sur les panneaux, un roulement usé et une résistance croissante dans un connecteur de batterie Après la tempête, une caméra portée sur la tête a lu les plaques et les codes d'alarme, puis un processeur local les a comparés au manuel hors ligne Aucune image sensible n'a éte envoyée dans le nuage Le logiciel exigeait que l'étiquette entière reste dans une marge süre, il contrôlait aussi la netteté générale et celle de la partie supérieure Une consigne sonore demandait de reculer si un bord manquait, et quatre images stables étaient nécessaires. Les ingenieurs ont ensuite confirme l'ordre proposé: nettoyer les panneaux, remplacer le roulement puis resserrer le connecteur. L'intervention a duré six minutes sans interrompre un service critique Une automatisation fiable 10 doit reconnaitre l'incertitude et laisser la décision finale a l'opérateur
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a hard-to-reach plateau, one station feeds a dispensary, a radio relay, weather instruments and safety lighting. The microgrid is made up of solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator. As the road may be closed for several days, a controller measures voltage, current, temperature and vibrations every 200 milliseconds. Detailed data remains on-site; only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational. Medical equipment and communications are a priority. On 18 October 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in fifteen minutes The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 8 °C, while the inverter fan produced an abnormal vibration Instead of shutting down the station, the system cut off the secondary heating, reduced some lighting and started the rescue group. He identified three possible causes of debris on the panels, a worn-out bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector. After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes, then a local processor compared them to the offline manual No sensitive image was sent to the cloud The software required the entire label to remain within a certain timeframe, it also controlled the overall sharpness and that of the top part A voice command asked to back off if an edge was missing, and four stable frames were needed. The engineers then confirmed the proposed order: clean the panels, replace the bearing, and tighten the connector. The intervention lasted six minutes without interrupting a critical service A reliable automation 10 must recognize the uncertainty and leave the final decision to the operator

The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly. and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation. where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation. and speech synthesis are performed. The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents. avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted. partly shadowed or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

It locates groups of text, estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still or improve the lighting

SOURCE     : After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction, edge-preserving fitering and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page, pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection. and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation where text detection, optical character recognition, language translation and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents. avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. hold still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters, while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes. For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Field evaluation of wearable translation glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a phone or searching through menus. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right. Hold it still. or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition. For that reason. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement, mild gamma correction, edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count, recognition confidence, focus statistics, and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone

Document Recognition System Modern document-reading systems combine optical character recognition with layout analysis. OCR identifies printed words, while layout models determine how information is arranged on the page. Tables require special processing because their meaning depends on rows, columns and headers. The following table summarizes the main processing modules used in a typical intelligent reading pipeline. Module Function Output PaddleOCR Recognizes printed text Text Table Detector Finds table regions Bounding box Structure Model Finds rows and columns Table layout RoBERTa Answers text questions Answer Table 1 Main modules of the document-processing pipeline System Operation After a page is captured, OCR extracts the visible words. If a table is detected, the table region is processed separately so that individual values remain associated with the correct headings. This structured representation can later be translated, searched or converted into speech. Preserving the document structure therefore makes spoken output easier for a user to understand.

EXTRACTED TEXT:
Surveillance autonome d'une station énergétique isolée Sur un plateau difficile d'accès, une station alimente un dispensaire un relais radio, des instruments météorologiques et l'éclairage de sécurité Le micro-réseau réunit des panneaux solaires, des batteries au lithium et un petit générateur diesel. Comme la route peut rester fermée plusieurs jours, un contrôleur mesure la tension, le courant, la température et les vibrations toutes les 200 millisecondes. Les données détaillées restent sur place; seul un résumé compressé est transmis lorsque la liaison fonctionne Les équipements médicaux et de communication sont prioritaires Le 18 octobre 2025, une tempête de poussière a réduit la production solaire de 34 % en quinze minutes. La température de l'armoire de batteries a augmenté de 8 °C, tandis que le ventilateur de l'onduleur produisait une vibration anormale Au lieu d'arrêter la station, le système a coupé le chauffage secondaire, réduit certains éclairages et démarré le groupe de secours. Il a identifié trois causes possibles des débris sur les panneaux, un roulement usé et une résistance croissante dans un connecteur de batterie Après la tempête, une caméra portée sur la tête a lu les plaques et les codes d'alarme, puis un processeur local les a comparés au manuel hors ligne Aucune image sensible n'a été envoyée dans le nuage. Le logiciel exigeait que l'étiquette entière reste dans une marge súre; il contrôlait aussi la netteté générale et celle de la partie supérieure Une consigne sonore demandait de reculer si un bord manquait, et quatre images stables étaient nécessaires Les ingénieurs ont ensuite confirmé l'ordre proposé nettoyer les panneaux, remplacer le roulement, puis resserrer le connecteur L'intervention a duré six minutes sans reconnaitre l'incertitude et laisser la décision finale a l'opérateur.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a hard-to-reach plateau, a station feeds a clinic with a radio relay, weather instruments and safety lighting The micro-grid includes solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator. Since the road can remain closed for days, a controller measures voltage, current, temperature and vibration every 200 milliseconds. Detailed data remains in place; only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational Medical and communication equipment is a priority On October 18, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34 percent in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery cabinet rose by 8°C, while the inverter fan produced an abnormal vibration. Instead of shutting down the station, the system turned off the secondary heating, reduced some of the lighting and started the rescue group. He identified three possible causes of debris on the panels, a worn-out bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector. After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes, then a local processor matched them to the offline manual. The software required that the entire label remain within a clear margin; it also controlled the overall sharpness and that of the top part A sound command asked to back up if an edge was missing, and four stable images were needed The engineers then confirmed the proposed order to clean the panels, replace the bearing, and then tighten the connector The intervention lasted six minutes without recognizing the uncertainty and leaving the final decision to the operator.

The software required that the entire label remain within a clear margin; it also controlled the overall sharpness and that of the top part A sound command asked to back up if an edge was missing, and four stable images were needed The engineers then confirmed the proposed order to clean the panels, replace the bearing, and then tighten the connector The intervention lasted six minutes without recognizing the uncertainty and leaving the final decision to the operator.

Preserving the document structure therefore makes spoken output easier for a user to understand.

TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a difficult-to-reach plateau, a station feeds a dispensary a radio relay, weather instruments and safety lighting The micro-network brings together solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator As the road may remain closed for several days, a controller measures the voltage, current. temperature and vibration every 200 milliseconds. Detailed data remains in place: only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational Medical and communication equipment is a priority On October 18, 2025, a dust storm reduced solar output by 34 percent in fifteen minutes. The temperature of the battery compartment has risen by 8°C. While the inverter fan was producing an abnormal vibration instead of shutting down the station. The system turned off the secondary heating, reduced some of the lights and started the rescue group. He identified three possible causes of the debris on the panels, a worn bearing and increasing resistance in a battery connector. After the storm, a head-worn camera read the license plates and alarm codes, then a local processor compared them to the offline manual.

EXTRACTED TEXT:
Paragraph-Level Translation and Spoken Guidance Reading a complete translated page as uninterrupted speech creates a serious usability problem. The listener hears the meaning but cannot tell which original line or paragraph is currently being spoken. This becomes especially confusing on technical documents containing warnings, numbered procedures labels, and tables. A wearable translator should preserve the connection between physical text and audio. The processing pipeline therefore retains the coordinates returned by optical character recognition and groups nearby lines into meaningful regions Each region becomes a separate translation unit instead of sending the entire page to the language model at once Reading order is determined from position, alignment, and spacing Lines that share a similar left edge and remain within a reasonable vertical distance are combined Large gaps, headings, bullet points, and changes in indentation begin new groups The original coordinates remain attached to every translated sentence During development, the selected paragraph is surrounded by a coloured box in the preview. In the wearable version, a short tone and a spoken paragraph number announce the same transition. The user can move forward, go back, repeat, pause, or stop with a small physical control or a limited voice command set Speech is generated only after a paragraph passes basic checks Empty results and very low recognition confidence request another image Extremely long regions are divided at sentence boundaries, while short neighbouring lines may be joined so the voice does not pause after every label fragment Numbers, units, dates and warning symbols receive special attention because a fluent sentence can still be dangerous when source paragraph first and the translated paragraph second This to notice recognition mistakes before acting on the result
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Paragraph-level translation and spoken guidance Reading a complete translated page as uninterrupted speech creates a serious usability problem. The listener hears the meaning but cannot tell which original line or paragraph is currently being spoken. This becomes especially confusing on technical documents containing warnings, numbered procedures labels, and tables. A wearable translator should preserve the connection between physical text and audio. The processing pipeline therefore retains the coordinates returned by optical character recognition and groups nearby lines into meaningful regions Each region becomes a separate translation unit instead of sending the entire page to the language model at once Reading order is determined from position, alignment, and spacing Lines that share a similar left edge and remain within a reasonable vertical distance are combined Large gaps, headings, bullet points, and changes in indentation begin new groups The original coordinates remain attached to every translated sentence During development, the selected paragraph is surrounded by a coloured box in the preview. In the wearable version, a short tone and a spoken paragraph number announce the same transition. The user can move forward, go back, repeat, pause, or stop with a small physical control or a limited voice command set Speech is generated only after a paragraph passes basic checks Empty results and very low recognition confidence request another image Extremely long regions are divided at sentence boundaries, while short neighbouring lines may be joined so the voice does not pause after every label fragment Numbers, units, dates and warning symbols receive special attention because a fluent sentence can still be dangerous when source paragraph first and the translated paragraph second This to notice recognition mistakes before acting on the result

OCR identifies printed words, while layout models determine how information is arranged on the page Tables require special processing because their meaning depends on rows, columns and headers. The following table summarizes the main processing modules used in a typical intelligent reading pipeline. Output Module Function PaddleOCR Recognizes printed text Text Table Detector Finds table regions Bounding box Structure Model Finds rows and columns Table layout Answer RoBERTa Answers text questions Table 1 Main modules of the document-processing pipeline System Operation After a page is captured, OCR extracts the visible words. Preserving the document structure therefore makes spoken output easier for a user to understand

EXTRACTED TEXT:
Field Evaluation of Wearable Translation Glasses A wearable translation system is most useful when it behaves like an ordinary tool rather than a laboratory demonstration. The user should be able to face a printed page. pause briefly, and hear a clear rendering without holding a telephone or searching through menus. In the prototype described here, a small camera is mounted near eye level and connected to a compact computer. Video is sent over a local link to a processing workstation, where text detection. optical character recognition, language translation, and speech synthesis are performed The complete pipeline operates without a cloud service This arrangement protects sensitive documents, avoids delays caused by an unstable internet connection and allows every software component to be measured independently Image acquisition is the first major difficulty. A person wearing glasses cannot easily see whether all four edges of a page are inside the camera view. The page may be tilted, partly shadowed, or closer at the top than at the bottom Motion from breathing and head movement also creates blur The capture controller therefore examines every incoming frame before saving it It locates groups of text. estimates whether the document occupies a useful fraction of the image, and checks that a safe border remains around the detected region. Sharpness is measured over the whole frame and again over the upper portion, because a slanted sheet often appears clear near the bottom while the first lines remain soft A frame is accepted only after several consecutive observations agree Spoken prompts tell the wearer to step back, move left or right, hold still, or improve the lighting After capture, the image is converted to grayscale and corrected only when the correction improves measured recognition Excessive sharpening can create bright halos around letters. while aggressive thresholding can erase punctuation and thin strokes For that reason. several preprocessing alternatives are tested on the same stored photographs. The comparison includes raw grayscale, local contrast enhancement. mild gamma correction. edge-preserving filtering. and adaptive binarization Each alternative is evaluated using character count. recognition confidence. focus statistics. and processing time Ground-truth text is retained for important experiments so that character error rate and word error rate can be calculated instead of relying on confidence alone
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Paragraph-Level Translation and Spoken Guidance Reading a complete translated page as uninterrupted speech creates a serious usability problem. The listener hears the meaning but cannot tell which original line or paragraph is currently being spoken This becomes especially confusing on technical documents containing warnings. numbered procedures. labels, and tables A wearable translator should preserve the connection between physical text and audio The processing pipeline therefore retains the coordinates returned by optical character recognition and groups nearby lines into meaningful regions Each region becomes a separate translation unit instead of sending the entire page to the language model at once Reading order is determined from position, alignment. and spacing. Lines that share a similar left edge and remain within a reasonable vertical distance are combined Large gaps. headings, bullet points, and changes in indentation begin new groups The original coordinates remain attached to every translated sentence During development. the selected paragraph is surrounded by a coloured box in the preview In the wearable version, a short tone and a spoken paragraph number announce the same transition The user can move forward, go back, repeat, pause, or stop with a small physical control or a limited voice command set Speech is generated only after a paragraph passes basic checks. Empty results and very low recognition confidence request another image Extremely long regions are divided at sentence boundaries, while short neighbouring lines may be joined so the voice does not pause after every label fragment Numbers. units. dates. and warning symbols receive special attention because a fluent sentence can still be dangerous when one measurement is wrong The interface can optionally read the source paragraph first and the translated paragraph second This slower mode helps during evaluation and allows bilingual users to notice recognition mistakes before acting on the result

偏远地区混合能源站的自主监测与维护 一座高原试验站依靠太阳能阵列、锂电池和小型柴油发电机供电。微电 网需要持续支持诊所、无线电中继、气象设备和安全照明。冬季道路可能 封闭数日，网络也不稳定，因此本地控制器每二百毫秒采集电压、电流、 温度与振动数据，并在能源不足时优先保障医疗和通信负载。完整记录保 存在站内，只有压缩后的状态摘要会在链路恢复时发送到控制中心。 二〇二五年十月十八日，一场沙尘风暴使太阳能输出在十五分钟内下降 百分之三十四，电池柜温度升高八摄氏度，逆变器风扇还出现异常低频振 动。控制器没有关闭整座电站，而是断开非必要加热装置、降低部分照明 功率并启动备用发电机。诊断模块随后提出三个可能原因太阳能板被碎 屑遮挡、风扇轴承磨损，以及电池连接器的接触电阻上升。 风暴减弱后，技术员用头戴式摄像设备读取铭牌、序列号和报警代码， 本地处理单元再与离线维护手册进行比对。由干资料涉及关键基础设施 图像没有上传云端。采集程序先确认整个标签位干安全边界内，并分别检 查全图和上部区域的清晰度若画面被裁切，耳机会提示向左、向右或向 后移动。目标只有连续四帧稳定且文字足够清楚时才会保存。第二天的日 志表明，自动排序与人工判断一致：先清理面板，再更换风扇轴承，最后 紧固电池端子。处置用了六分钟，关键服务未中断。这说明可靠的自动化 必须解释判断、承认不确定性，并把最终决定留给人。

TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Autonomous monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in remote areas A plateau test station relies on solar arrays, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Micro-grids need to continue to support clinics, radio relay, weather equipment and safety lighting. Roads can be closed for days in winter and the network is unstable, so local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and vibration data every 200 milliseconds, and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. The complete record is stored on the station, and only the compressed status summary is sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2025, a dust storm caused a 34 percent drop in solar output in fifteen minutes, a temperature rise of eight degrees Celsius in the battery cabinet, and an abnormally low frequency vibration in the inverter fan. Instead of shutting down the entire power plant, the controller disconnects unnecessary heating devices, lowers the power of some lighting and starts the backup generator. Diagnostic modules then suggested three possible reasons for the shredded solar panels, fan bearing wear, and increased contact resistance of the battery connector. After the storm weakened, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the insignia, serial numbers and alarm codes, and the local processing unit was compared to the offline maintenance manual. Images of critical infrastructure are not uploaded to the cloud due to interference. The retriever first identifies the entire label as being within the safe boundary and checks the clarity of the entire image and the upper region separately if the image is cropped, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four lines is stable and the text is clear enough. The next day's logs showed that the automatic sorting was consistent with the artificial judgment: first the panels were cleaned, then the fan bearings were replaced, and finally the battery terminals were tightened. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must interpret judgments, acknowledge uncertainty, and leave the final decision to humans.

偏远地区混合能源站的自主监测与维护 一座高原试验站依靠太阳能阵列、锂电池和小型柴油发电机供电。微电 网需要持续支持诊所、无线电中继、气象设备和安全照明。冬季道路可能 封闭数日，网络也不稳定，因此本地控制器每二百毫秒采集电压、电流、 温度与振动数据，并在能源不足时优先保障医疗和通信负载。完整记录保 存在站内只有压缩后的状态摘要会在链路恢复时发送到控制中心。 二〇二五年十月十八日，一场沙尘风暴使太阳能输出在十五分钟内下降 百分之三十四电池柜温度升高八摄氏度，逆变器风扇还出现异常低频振 动。控制器没有关闭整座电站，而是断开非必要加热装置、降低部分照明 功率并启动各用发电机。诊断模块随后提出三个可能原因：太阳能板被碎 肩遮挡、风扇轴承磨损以及电池连接器的接触电阻上升。 风暴减弱后，技术员用头戴式摄像设备读取铭牌、序列号和报警代码. 本地处理单元再与离线维护手册进行比对。由于资料涉及关键基础设施 图像没有上传云端。采集程序先确认整个标签位于安全边界内，并分别检 查全图和上部区域的清晰度：若画面被载切，耳机会提示向左、向右或向 后移动。目标只有连续四帧稳定且文字足够清楚时才会保存。第二天的日 志表明，自动排序与人工判断一致先清理面板，再更换风扇轴承，最后 紧固电池端子。处置用了六分钟，关键服务未中断。这说明可靠的自动化 必须解释判断、承认不确定性，并把最终决定留给人。

TRANSLATED TEXT (ENGLISH):
Autonomous monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in remote areas A plateau test station relies on solar arrays, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Micro-grids need to continue to support clinics, radio relay, weather equipment and safety lighting. Roads can be closed for days in winter and the network is unstable, so local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and vibration data every 200 milliseconds, and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. Complete records are stored at the station and only compressed status summaries are sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2025, a dust storm caused solar output to drop by 34 percent in fifteen minutes, the temperature of the battery cabinet to rise eight degrees Celsius, and the inverter fan to vibrate at an abnormally low frequency. Instead of shutting down the entire power plant, the controller disconnects unnecessary heating devices, lowers the power of some lighting and starts up the various generators. Diagnostic modules then suggested three possible causes: the solar panels were shrouded by broken shoulders, fan bearing wear, and the contact resistance of the battery connector was elevated. After the storm subsided, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the insignia, serial numbers and alarm codes. The local processing unit is then compared to the offline maintenance manual. Images of critical infrastructure are not uploaded to the cloud. The capture process first confirms that the entire label is within the safe boundary and checks the clarity of the entire image and the upper region separately: if the image is cut, the earpiece is prompted to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four lines is stable and the text is clear enough. The next day's logs showed that the automatic sorting was consistent with the artificial judgment of cleaning the panels, replacing the fan bearings, and finally tightening the battery terminals. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must interpret judgments, acknowledge uncertainty, and leave the final decision to humans.

Autonomous monitoring and maintenance of hybrid power stations in remote areas A plateau test station relies on solar arrays, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator to power it. Micro-grids need to continue to support clinics, radio relay, weather equipment and safety lighting. Roads can be closed for days in winter and the network is unstable, so local controllers collect voltage, current, temperature and vibration data every 200 milliseconds, and prioritize medical and communications loads when energy is scarce. The complete record is stored on the station, and only the compressed status summary is sent to the control center when the link is restored. On October 18, 2025, a dust storm caused a 34 percent drop in solar output in fifteen minutes, a temperature rise of eight degrees Celsius in the battery cabinet, and an abnormally low frequency vibration in the inverter fan. Instead of shutting down the entire power plant, the controller disconnects unnecessary heating devices, lowers some lighting and starts a backup generator. Diagnostic modules then suggested three possible reasons for the shredded solar panels, fan bearing wear, and increased contact resistance of the battery connector. After the storm subsided, technicians used head-mounted cameras to read the insignia, serial numbers and alarm codes. The local processing unit is then compared to the offline maintenance manual. Images of critical infrastructure are not uploaded to the cloud. The capture process first identifies the entire label as being within the security boundary and checks the clarity of the entire image and the upper region separately if the image is loaded with a headset that prompts it to move left, right or backwards. The target is saved only when the sequence of four lines is stable and the text is clear enough. The next day's logs showed that the automatic sorting was consistent with the artificial judgment: first the panels were cleaned, then the fan bearings were replaced, and finally the battery terminals were tightened. The disposal took six minutes and critical services were not interrupted. This shows that reliable automation must interpret judgments, acknowledge uncertainty, and leave the final decision to humans.

Surveillance autonome d'une station énergétique isolée Sur un plateau difficile d'accès, une station alimente un dispensaire. un relais radio. des instruments météorologiques et l'éclairage de sécurité Le micro-réseau réunit des panneaux solaires, des batteries au lithium et un petit générateur diesel. Comme la route peut rester fermée plusieurs jours, un contrôleur mesure la tension, le courant. la température et les vibrations toutes les 200 millisecondes. Les données détaillées restent sur place; seul un résumé compressé est transmis lorsque la liaison fonctionne Les équipements médicaux et de communication sont prioritaires Le 18 octobre 2025. une tempête de poussière a réduit la production solaire de 34 % en quinze minutes. La température de l'armoire de batteries a augmenté de 8 °C. tandis que le ventilateur de l'onduleur produisait une vibration anormale. Au lieu d'arrêter la station, le système a coupé le chauffage secondaire, réduit certains éclairages et démarré le groupe de secours Il a identifié trois causes possibles des débris sur les panneaux, un roulement usé et une résistance croissante dans un connecteur de batterie Après la tempête, une caméra portée sur la tête a lu les plaques et les codes d'alarme. puis un processeur local les a comparès au manuel hors ligne Aucune image sensible n'a été envoyée dans le nuage. Le logiciel exigeait que l'étiquette entière reste dans une marge sure, il contrôlait aussi la netteté générale et celle de la partie supérieure. Une consigne sonore demandait de reculer si un bord manquait, et quatre images stables étaient nécessaires. Les ingénieurs ont ensuite confirmé l'ordre proposé nettoyer les panneaux, remplacer le roulement, puis resserrer le connecteur. L'intervention a duré six minutes sans interrompre un service critique Une automatisation fiable doit reconnaitre l'incertitude et laisser la décision finale à l'opérateur

Self-monitoring of an isolated power station On a hard-to-reach shelf, a station feeds a dispensary. It's a radio relay. The micro-grid includes solar panels, lithium batteries and a small diesel generator. Since the road can remain closed for days, a controller measures the voltage, the current. temperature and vibrations every 200 milliseconds. Detailed data remains in place; only a compressed summary is transmitted when the link is operational Medical and communication equipment is a priority It's the 18th of October 2025. A dust storm reduced solar output by 34% in 15 minutes. The temperature of the battery compartment has risen by 8°C. While the inverter fan was producing an abnormal vibration. Instead of shutting down the station, the system turned off the secondary heating, reduced some of the lights, and started the rescue group. It identified three possible causes of the debris on the panels, a worn-out bearing, and increasing resistance in a battery connector. After the storm, a head-mounted camera read the license plates and alarm codes. And then a local processor compared them to the offline manual. No sensitive images were sent to the cloud. The software required that the entire label remain within a safe margin, and it also controlled the overall sharpness and that of the upper part. A sound signal was given to back up if a edge was missing, and four steady frames were needed. The engineers then confirmed the proposed order to clean the panels, replace the bearing, and then tighten the connector. The intervention lasted six minutes without interrupting a critical service reliable automation must recognize uncertainty and leave the final decision to the operator

EN16-01- Calibrating Portable Air-Quality Sensors A teaching laboratory received twelve portable air-quality monitors for a field course on indoor ventilation. Before students could use them, the instruments had to be checked against the laboratory reference station The monitors measured carbon dioxide, temperature and relative humidity, and they were expected to agree closely enough for comparative surveys. On 8 September 2026, the technician placed all units on the same bench for forty minutes so that their temperature could stabilize. Windows were kept closed, no one stood directly beside the sensors, and the reference station logged one reading every 30 seconds. Morning Calibration Sequence The first comparison showed that most carbon-dioxide readings were within 35 ppm of the reference, but two monitors differed by more than 90 ppm. Their humidity channels also responded slowly after a brief change in room conditions. Rather than applying a correction immediately, the technician inspected the intake openings and found a thin layer of packing dust on both units. After cleaning the vents with dry air and repeating the stabilization period, the large offsets disappeared The event was recorded because it demonstrated that a poor result can come from handling and storage rather than from a failed serising element For the final check, the room was occupied by six students for fifteen minutes, raising the carbon-dioxide level from approximately 510 ppm to 1,120 ppm. Each monitor had to follow the rise and fall without sudden steps or frozen values. The reference unit remained on mains power. while the portable units ran on their internal batteries. The slowest sensor reached 90% of the reference change in 74 seconds, the fastest required 41 seconds. These response times were acceptable for the planned room-to-room survey, which focused on ventilation trends rather than second-by-second exposure. The calibration record was printed and attached to the equipment case Students were instructed to repeat a short co-location check before every major field session and to note any unusual delay, battery warning or blocked vent The procedure did not turn inexpensive monitors into laboratory instruments, but it established a traceable baseline for the course More importantly, it gave students a clear example of why measurement quality depends on preparation, environmental control and careful documentation, not only on the number shown on a display

EN16-01- Calibrating Portable Air-Quality Sensors A teaching laboratory received twelve portable air-quality monitors for a field course on indoor ventilation. Before students could use them, the instruments had to be checked against the laboratory reference station. The monitors measured carbon dioxide, temperature and relative humidity, and they were expected to agree closely enough for comparative surveys. On 8 September 2026, the technician placed all units on the same bench for forty minutes so that their temperature could stabilize, Windows were kept closed, no one stood directly beside the sensors, and the reference station logged one reading every 30 seconds Morning Calibration Sequence The first comparison showed that most carbon-dioxide readings were within 35 ppm of the reference, but two monitors differed by more than 90 ppm. Their humidity channels also responded slowly after a brief change in room conditions. Rather than applying a correction immediately, the technician inspected the intake openings and found a thin layer of packing dust on both units. After cleaning the vents with dry air and repeating the stabilization period, the large offsets disappeared. The event was recorded because it demonstrated that a poor result can come from handling and storage rather than from a failed sensing element For the final check, the room was occupied by six students for fifteen minutes, raising the carbon-dioxide level from approximately 510 ppm to 1,120 ppm. Each monitor had to follow the rise and fall without sudden steps or frozen values. The reference unit remained on mains power, while the portable units ran on their internal batteries. The slowest sensor reached 90% of the reference change in 74 seconds; the fastest required 41 seconds. These response times were acceptable for the planned room-to-room survey, which focused on ventilation trends rather than second-by-second exposure. The calibration record was printed and attached to the equipment case. Students were instructed to repeat a short co-location check before every major field session and to note any unusual delay, battery warning or blocked vent. The procedure did not turn inexpensive monitors into laboratory instruments, but it established a traceable baseline for the course. More importantly, it gave students a clear example of why measurement quality depends on preparation, environmental control and careful documentation, not only on the number shown on a display

EN16-02 - Planning a Small Observatory Night Shift The university astronomy club planned a four-hour observing session for 21 October 2026 at a hilltop site outside the city. The goal was not to collect publishable research data, but to train new members in safe telescope setup. sky navigation and log keeping. Sunset was expected shortly after 17:40, so the equipment team scheduled arrival for 16:50. This left enough daylight to inspect tripods, route power cables and confirm that the emergency lamps worked before the observing area became dark. Weather forecasts from three services disagreed about the amount of high cloud. One predicted 20% cloud cover, another 45%, and the local station suggested thin cloud would arrive after 21:00. The club therefore chose targets that could be observed in a flexible order. Bright objects. including Jupiter and several double stars, were placed early in the plan. Fainter nebulae were listed as optional. A small digital thermometer and hygrometer would record conditions every twenty minutes, because dew formation on optical surfaces was considered a greater operational risk than moderate high cloud. Roles and Safety Checks New members were divided into three pairs. One pair handled the 200 mm reflector, one operated the smaller refractor, and the third maintained the written observing log and checked red-light discipline. Every forty minutes the roles would rotate. Nobody was allowed to move a tripod without first announcing the movement, and food was kept away from the optical tables. The organizers also marked a two-metre clear path between the instruments and the vehicles so that people could leave safely without stepping over cases or cables. The session plan included a simple cancellation rule. If wind remained above 35 km/h for ten minutes, if rain was detected, or if visibility on the access road became poor, the group would pack immediately. A successful night was defined as safe practice and complete logs, not the number of objects seen By setting that expectation in advance, the club reduced pressure to continue in marginal conditions and gave beginners a structured introduction to field observing. A paper checklist at the counted before the group left the site

EN16-03 - Measuring Quiet Zones in a Public Library Survey Method A public library wanted to understand why visitors described one reading room as quiet even when the sound meter showed levels similar to those in another room. Staff designed a short acoustic survey using a calibrated handheld meter and a written observation sheet. Measurements were taken at five marked positions during three periods of the day The meter was mounted 1.2 m above the floor and kept at least 1 m from walls or large furniture. Each sample lasted sixty seconds and recorded both the average sound level and the highest short-duration peak The morning survey produced averages between 36.8 and 39 5 dBA During the afternoon, the values rose by roughly 4 dB as more people used the study tables. The highest peak, 61.2 dBA, occurred when a metal water bottle fell near the entrance. Surprisingly, the room that visitors considered calmer did not always have the lowest average level Observers noted that its sounds were more continuous: ventilation noise, turning pages and distant footsteps. In the other room, sudden chair movements and brief conversations were more noticeable even when the overall average remained modest. Staff used the observations to test small changes rather than imposing strict silence rules. Felt pads were added to twenty-four chair legs, a return trolley was moved away from the main reading area, and a soft- close strip was fitted to one cabinet door One week later the same measurement route was repeated Average levels changed only slightly. but the number of peaks above 55 dBA fell from seventeen to nine during the busiest hour. Visitor comments also mentioned fewer abrupt interruptions The survey showed that a single average number could not describe the entire experience of a space Frequency, timing and character of sounds also mattered The library therefore kept the simple route as a quarterly check and added a column for notable sound events This gave staff a repeatable way to evaluate practical changes without treating the sound meter as a complete measure of comfort The same marked positions were retained on a floor plan so that future measurements could be taken at comparable locations rather than wherever space happened to be available
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Surprisingly, the room that visitors considered calmer did not always have the lowest average level Observers noted that its sounds were more continuous: ventilation noise, turning pages and distant footsteps. In the other room, sudden chair movements and brief conversations were more noticeable even when the overall average remained modest. Staff used the observations to test small changes rather than imposing strict silence rules. Felt pads were added to twenty-four chair legs, a return trolley was moved away from the main reading area, and a soft- close strip was fitted to one cabinet door One week later the same measurement route was repeated Average levels changed only slightly. but the number of peaks above 55 dBA fell from seventeen to nine during the busiest hour. Visitor comments also mentioned fewer abrupt interruptions The survey showed that a single average number could not describe the entire experience of a space Frequency, timing and character of sounds also mattered The library therefore kept the simple route as a quarterly check and added a column for notable sound events This gave staff a repeatable way to evaluate practical changes without treating the sound meter as a complete measure of comfort The same marked positions were retained on a floor plan so that future measurements could be taken at comparable locations rather than wherever space happened to be available

EN12-01 - Managing Emergency Water Storage on a Campus reserve, but it did not specify how often containers should be inspected or who was responsible for replacing them. A working group therefore mapped the locations of tanks, portable containers and drinking-water dispensers across eight buildings. The review focused on short interruptions lasting less than one day, because longer emergencies would require outside supply and a different distribution plan Storage and Inspection Rules The group estimated a minimum planning quantity of 3 litres of drinking water per person for a 24- hour period, with additional water needed for basic hygiene and food preparation Rather than filling every available container, staff selected food-grade vessels that could be sealed, labelled and moved safely Each label showed the fill date, intended use and responsible building. Containers were kept away from direct sunlight, cleaning chemicals and fuel. The largest portable vessel weighed almost 24 kg when full, so it was placed on a low trolley instead of a high shelf Inspection became the most important part of the new plan On the first Monday of every month, a building representative checked seals, leaks, labels and storage conditions Any container with a damaged cap, unusual odour or unclear history was emptied and cleaned rather than kept for convenience. The fixed tanks were included in the facilities maintenance schedule, with records of cleaning dates and inlet-screen condition A small sample of stored water was also checked after long periods of non-use according to the campus health office procedure. A short exercise was held on 14 August 2026. One residence floor was told that tap water was unavailable for two hours, and volunteers practised retrieving, carrying and issuing the stored supply. The exercise revealed that the written map was accurate but one trolley could not pass through a narrow service doorway Moving two containers to a different room solved the problem The group also learned that people needed clear instructions about which reserve was suitable for drinking and which was intended only for cleaning. The final plan treated stored water as a managed resource rather than a pile of containers. It assigned ownership, inspection intervals. safe lifting arrangements and a method for recording use The reserve was modest, but the process reduced confusion during routine interruptions and provided a stronger starting point for larger emergency planning.

EN12-01 - Managing Emergency Water Storage on a Campus A residential campus reviewed its emergency water plan after a scheduled pipeline repair lasted longer than expected. The existing guidance stated that each residence block should keep a small reserve, but it did not specify how often containers should be inspected or who was responsible for replacing them. A working group therefore mapped the locations of tanks. portable containers and drinking-water dispensers across eight buildings. The review focused on short interruptions lasting less than one day, because longer emergencies would require outside supply and a different distribution plan Storage and Inspection Rules The group estimated a minimum planning quantity of 3 litres of drinking water per person for a 24- hour period, with additional water needed for basic hygiene and food preparation. Rather than filling every available container, staff selected food-grade vessels that could be sealed, labelled and moved safely Each label showed the fill date, intended use and responsible building. Containers were kept away from direct sunlight, cleaning chemicals and fuel. The largest portable vessel weighed almost 24 kg when full, so it was placed on a low trolley instead of a high shelf Inspection became the most important part of the new plan. On the first Monday of every month, a building representative checked seals, leaks, labels and storage conditions. Any container with a damaged cap, unusual odour or unclear history was emptied and cleaned rather than kept for convenience The fixed tanks were included in the facilities maintenance schedule, with records of cleaning dates and inlet-screen condition A small sample of stored water was also checked after long periods of non-use according to the campus health office procedure A short exercise was held on 14 August 2026 One residence floor was told that tap water was unavailable for two hours, and volunteers practised retrieving, carrying and issuing the stored supply The exercise revealed that the written map was accurate but one trolley could not pass through a narrow service doorway Moving two containers to a different room solved the problem The group also learned that people needed clear instructions about which reserve was suitable for managed resource rather than a pile of containers. It assigned ownership, inspection intervals. safe lifting arrangements and a method for recording use. The reserve was modest. but the process reduced confusion during routine interruptions and provided a stronger starting point for larger emergency planning

EN12-02 - A Pilot Bicycle Counter on a Campus Road A transport research class installed a temporary bicycle counter on a campus road to compare manual observations with an electronic sensing system. The site was chosen because it carred steady bicycle traffic but had only one vehicle lane in each direction, making visual verification practical Two students marked a 12 m observation zone with removable tape and positioned the sensor so that passing bicycles crossed its detection area at a consistent angle. Data collection began at 07 30 on 3 September 2026 and continued until 18:30. For validation, observers counted bicycles manually during six separate thirty-minute windows They recorded direction, bicycle type and whether two riders passed side by side The electronic counter stored a timestamp and direction estimate for every detected event. During the moming period. the system counted 146 bicycles while the observers counted 150 Review of the uimestamps showed that most missed events occurred when pairs travelled close together A second issue appeared when a grounds vehicle moved slowly along the edge of the detection zone and produced two false bicycle events. Installation Adjustment The class adjusted the installation rather than changing the data after collection. The sensor was rotated by 7 degrees and moved 0.6 m farther from the road edge so that maintenance vehicles were less likely to enter its strongest detection region. The next validation window produced 132 electronic counts against 134 manual counts. Side-by-side riders still presented a challenge. but the false vehicle detections stopped. Students noted that a small numerical improvement was useful only because the physical reason for the change was understood and documented Daily traffic patterns were also informative. The largest thirty-minute total occurred between 08 10 and 08 40, while a second peak appeared after classes ended. Rain beginning at 15:20 reduced bicycle traffic by approximately 38% compared with the previous dry hour. The class did not treat this single day as representative of an entire semester: instead, it used the exercise to practise installation, validation and uncertainty reporting. At the end of the pilot, all temporary markings were removed and the dataset was archived with a site photograph, sensor orientation sketch and calibration notes. The main lesson was that automated counters can reduce labour, but they sill require field checks. Without manual observations, the class would not have known whether an unusual count reflected real travel behaviour, a passing service vehicle or limitations in separating closely spaced riders

EN12-03 - Digitizing Handwritten Field Notebooks A small environmental archive began digitizing field notebooks created by survey teams between 1987 and 2004. The notebooks contained handwritten observations, sketches, pasted labels and occasional measurements written in pencil. Because the originals were unique. the project was designed around preservation first and speed second Every notebook received a temporary work number, and staff photographed its cover and condition before scanning. Pages with loose inserts were flagged so that no item would be lost when the binding was opened. The scanning station used an overhead camera rather than a flatbed scanner because several bindings could not be pressed safely. Pages were supported at a gentle angle and illuminaled by two diffuse lamps positioned to reduce glare. A grey reference card appeared in the first image of each session. Most pages were captured at 400 ppi equivalent resolution, while maps and pages containing very small annotations were recorded at higher resolution. Operators checked focus at the centre and corners before continuing through a notebook. File naming was deliberately simple. A notebook identified as FN-1994-17 produced images such as FN-1994-17_P001 and FN-1994-17_P002. If a loose insert belonged between pages 18 and 19. it received a suffix rather than forcing the rest of the sequence to be renamed A checksum was generated after transfer to the archive server, and a second copy was written to offline storage. The project log recorded the operator, capture date, equipment settings and any unusual page condition Access Copy Versus Original Evidence Text recognition was treated as an access aid, not a replacement for the image. Handwriting quality varied widely. and technical abbreviations often confused automated systems. Staff therefore created a short verified transcription only for titles, dates. locations and selected measurements Search users could find a notebook through those fields and then inspect the original page image. Where a number was uncertain, the transcription included a visible uncertainty marker rather than silently choosing a value By the end of the first month, 2,480 pages had been captured from thirly-six notebooks The team intentionally avoided setting a daily page quota because fragile material required different handling times. Instead. quality was reviewed through weekly sample checks of focus, sequence, colour reference and file integrity This slower but controlled workflow preserved the relationship between the digital files and the physical notebooks, which was more important than maximizing the number of scans completed each day
